sentences.text: Colymbosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur, a marine reptile, classified within the family Cryptoclididae.
The known fossil remains include 74 vertebrae, ribs, a scapula, and the front and rear flippers.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is simply a single humerus found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation of Oxfordshire, England.
The species C. svalbardensis was described from fossils discovered in the Agardhfjellet Formation of Svalbard, Norway, in the winter of 1930-31.
This animal was described by Harry Seeley in 1874 from fossils found in England.
A taxonomic revision led to the resurrection of C. megadeirus as the type species of Colymbosaurus after it was previously synonymized with C. trochantericus.
Colymbosaurus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic in the UK and Svalbard, Norway.
The time range for Colymbosaurus is estimated from 168.2 to 113.2 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Aptian stages.
Some scientists debate whether Colymbosaurus is actually part of Kimmerosaurus, a genus known only from skull and cervical vertebrae elements.
